**Construction:** let $x_n = 4\{n\sqrt{2}\}$ for $n \ge 0$, where $\{t\} = t - \lfloor t \rfloor$ is the fractional part.

**Boundedness:** $0 \le \{n\sqrt2\} < 1$, so $|x_n| \le 4$ for all $n$. Take $C = 4$.

**Key inequality:** Let $q = |i-j| \ge 1$. Then $d = \{i\sqrt2\} - \{j\sqrt2\}$ satisfies $|d| < 1$ and $d \equiv (i-j)\sqrt2 \pmod 1$. So $|d|$ is at least the distance from $q\sqrt2$ (or $-q\sqrt2$) to the nearest integer, i.e. $|d| \ge \|q\sqrt2\|$. Hence
$$|x_i - x_j| = 4|d| \ge 4\|q\sqrt2\|.$$

**Lower bound on $\|q\sqrt2\|$:** Let $p$ be an integer nearest to $q\sqrt2$, so $|q\sqrt2 - p| = \|q\sqrt2\| \le \tfrac12$. Since $\sqrt2$ is irrational and $p, q$ are integers with $q \ge 1$, $p^2 - 2q^2$ is a nonzero integer, so $|p^2 - 2q^2| \ge 1$. Therefore
$$\|q\sqrt2\| = \frac{|2q^2 - p^2|}{q\sqrt2 + p} \ge \frac{1}{q\sqrt2 + p}.$$
Since $p \le q\sqrt2 + \tfrac12$, we get $q\sqrt2 + p \le 2\sqrt2\,q + \tfrac12 \le 4q$ for $q \ge 1$. Hence $\|q\sqrt2\| \ge \dfrac{1}{4q}$, and so
$$|x_i - x_j| \ge \frac{1}{q}.$$

**Verification:** Since $a > 1$ and $q \ge 1$, we have $q^{a-1} \ge 1$, so
$$|x_i - x_j|\,|i-j|^a \ge \frac{1}{q}\cdot q^a = q^{a-1} \ge 1.$$

This holds for every pair of distinct nonnegative integers $i, j$, and the sequence is bounded. The construction works for every real $a > 1$.

ANSWER: $x_n = 4\{n\sqrt{2}\}$ (bounded by $C=4$), where $\{t\}$ denotes the fractional part of $t$.
